content.title: Johnson: Alabama, hire the Nick Saban of hardwood. For real this time.
content.text: This is an opinion column.Kristy Curry set the table.She stabilized women’s basketball at the University of Alabama following the retirement of longtime coach Rick Moody in 2005 and tepid tenures by Stephany Smith (27-61, 4-39 in SEC) and Wendell Hudson, the former Tide player who, in 1969, became the first African-American to receive an athletic scholarship at Alabama. As a head coach, he went 68-87 overall and 14-64 in conference play.Curry arrived in 2013 from Texas Tech, amassed a 245-173 record (88-120 in SEC) and guided the Tide to the NCAA tournament for the past four seasons, reaching the second round in each of the last three. Her teams snapped a 42-game losing streak against once-vaunted Tennessee and have beaten the Vols in 8 of their last 16 meetings.This week, Curry, 59, curiously walked away, leaving the Tide for South Florida, a mid-major. Alabama Athletic Director Greg Byrne termed her Crimson Tide tenure “commendable” on social media, a chilly compliment hinting there may be more to the departure than yet revealed.Nonetheless, the exit offers a unique opportunity for Byrne. The table is set for Alabama to build on Curry’s foundation and it’s up to him to deliver the next course.By hiring Dawn Staley.By hiring one of the best basketball coaches in the nation — female or male, college or pro.By hiring someone the Tide couldn’t quite persuade to come to Tuscaloosa more than two decades ago. Back then Staley was not yet a coaching icon at SEC rival South Carolina. Not quite yet a three-time national championship coach and six-time National Coach of the Year with 10 league titles (including this season) and seven Final Four appearances. She had not yet become the universally respected molder of young women, a bold and inspiring voice for Black women and the dynamic face of women’s basketball in an era of explosive growth and unprecedented popularity.Not quite yet. In 2005, and in only her 5th year at Temple, Staley was a leading candidate to replace Moody and remembers having a “great interview” with Mal Moore, who was the Alabama AD at the time.The southern vibe, however, didn’t mesh with the Philadelphia native. Not quite yet.“For me, I’m a feeler. I like to feel being in the place and seeing myself in the place and once I got to Alabama, no offense, I just didn’t feel myself,” Staley recalled last year in Birmingham during the 2025 Sweet 16. “I was so young. I’m from Philly, and I didn’t have an appreciation for the South at that point. Just too young and dumb to realize it.”Staley has obviously grown and matured and now embraces her status and power in the sport.“I’m doing what I’m supposed to be doing,” she shared last year. “I’m comfortable in my skin, with dealing with look, sound, feel. If something looks, sounds or feels off, then I address it. If it looks, sounds or feels great, then I promote it.”At least make the call, sir.She’s a bit busy right now. Her top-seeded Gamecocks face No. 4-seed Oklahoma Saturday in the Sweet 16 of the 2026 NCAA Tournament. And I’m under no delusion that luring her to Tuscaloosa will be any easier this time.It will certainly be expensive. In January 2025, Staley signed a historic four-year extension worth $25.25 million that runs through 2029-30 and makes her the highest-paid women’s coach ever. She earns $4 million annually with a $250,000 bump each season. If she leaves for another college job before the end of the contract, the buyout is the remaining amount. Let’s call it $9.5 million.To at least persuade Staley to think about coming to Tuscaloosa, I’d offer a salary on par with Nate Oats’s ($5.6 million in 2025), with a rider to match his salary should Byrne give him a raise to keep him there. She’s worth every dollar.Heck, should Oats bolt for North Carolina or elsewhere, offer Staley either team. Don’t even think about telling me she couldn’t coach men. That she can’t win with men, too.CLEVELAND, OHIO - APRIL 07: Head coach Dawn Staley of the South Carolina Gamecocks celebrates after beating the Iowa Hawkeyes in the 2024 NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament National Championship at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse on April 07, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. South Carolina beat Iowa 87-75. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images)Getty ImagesByrne certainly has a prolific array of intriguing and qualified options. Consider Joni Taylor, the former Tide player, now head coach at Texas A&M ; Alabama A&M’s Dawn E. Thornton, whose team just won the SWAC regular season title (her previous Arkansas Pine-Bluff team upset Arkansas); Megan Duffy (42-22 at Virginia Tech and 196-89 career); Chanda Rigby at Troy (280-165); or former Alabama player and long-time Shelton State coach Madonna Thompson (750+ wins).None of them is Staley. None would roll the Tide faithful like the top coach in the game. None is the Nick Saban of hardwood.The table is set. Make the call, sir. Get her.
